documents.title: GitKB onboarding and GitHub persistence
documents.content: Repository agents discover GitKB through the root AGENTS.md. README.md links https://gitkb.com/ and the official installation guide https://gitkb.com/docs/getting-started/installation/. On a fresh clone with an empty local KB, run: git-kb restore .kb/backups/bootstrap.json && git-kb code index --index-only src scripts tests docs wscript. Do not restore over newer local work. Git tracks configuration, agent guidance, and the portable backup; the mutable store, caches, and workspaces stay ignored. Commit KB documents first, refresh the backup with git-kb backup --output .kb/backups/bootstrap.json, and include it in the relevant Git commit. A GitKB commit alone does not update GitHub. See [[specs/reading-and-typography]] and [[context/overridable/current-state]].

documents.title: Bibble project brief
documents.content:
Bibble is a KJV Bible reader for Pebble Time 2 (emery) and Pebble Round 2 (gabbro). The native watch UI is C. Phone-side JavaScript (PKJS) downloads/caches the KJV corpus, handles dictation reference parsing and phrase search, and provides paginated content. The web settings page is maintained under `src/config` and generated under `docs/config` for hosting.

The user-approved reading and typography contract is [[specs/reading-and-typography]]. Existing build, deployment, and publishing documentation is imported at [[repo/readme]], [[repo/files/docs/publishing-md]], and [[repo/files/docs/app-store-listing-md]].

Code entry points: [[code:src/c/main.c]], [[code:src/pkjs/index.js]], [[code:src/pkjs/bible.js]], [[code:src/pkjs/search-index.js]], [[code:src/common/reader-layout.js]].

Repository inventory: [[context/extensible/repository-inventory]].

documents.title: Current implementation and verification state
documents.content:
Imported from Git revision `55236ff9ec2cbe30eba178856ea45c52f9771d1c`. Repository was clean before git-kb initialization; the chapter header change is now in Git as `55236ff`.

Current behavior is described by [[specs/reading-and-typography]]. Prior conversation verification covered unit tests, both watch builds, metric-based grid fitting, browser previews, and a compiled header-formatting harness. Final on-device rendering remains unverified in this session; do not translate metric/build success into a hardware guarantee. No deployment is authorized merely by this KB initialization.

Documentation discrepancy: the imported README still states that all selection grids use Gothic 24 Bold. The final code and user-approved requirement make book labels follow the selected profile, while chapter and verse grids retain 24 Bold. The README's reference to full round header references is also broader than current reader behavior, which uses compact book abbreviations. Imported documents are snapshots, not corrections of those statements.

For future changes, consult [[decisions/pagination-evolution]] before modifying pagination. Regenerate `docs/config` with `npm run build:config:docs`; run `npm test` and `npm run build:watch` as appropriate. Device installs are separate actions.

The KB is local, without a remote or embeddings configured. Reindex source after changes using `git-kb code index --index-only src scripts tests docs wscript`. Imported source snapshots have revision and SHA-256 provenance; refresh them intentionally rather than treating them as live mirrors.

documents.title: Why pagination uses geometry and whole verses
documents.content:
Final decision: measure glyph bounds against actual screen geometry and pack whole verses; only verses longer than an entire screen may continue across pages. See [[specs/reading-and-typography]].

Superseded attempts, retained to prevent regressions:
1. A fixed 135-character budget for 24 Bold split John 3:16 after "have", even though the whole verse fit.
2. Keeping a verse intact whenever it fit the reader's text buffer allowed content to extend below the visible screen at Very large. Existing scrolling did not satisfy the user's no-overflow requirement.
3. Geometry-based filling of every row could begin the next page halfway through a verse that would have fit a fresh screen. The user clarified that pages should begin with a new verse except for unavoidable continuation of an oversized verse.

Final precedence: no clipped lines; preserve verse boundaries whenever a verse fits a fresh screen; then maximize whole-verse packing within the available space. Unused rows at a verse boundary are intentional.

Source of authority: the user's successive clarifications in this conversation. These are not three alternative supported modes.

documents.content:
Source: `.github/workflows/pages.yml`

Git revision: `55236ff9ec2cbe30eba178856ea45c52f9771d1c`. SHA-256: `fa787c358e345743766fe64ceec06bfea1573d6e20fece5a21bfdb786fbc17c3`.

Snapshot imported during KB initialization. The repository file remains the editable source of truth.

````
name: Deploy Pages

on:
  push:
    branches:
      - master
  workflow_dispatch:

permissions:
  contents: read
  pages: write
  id-token: write

concurrency:
  group: deploy-pages
  cancel-in-progress: true

jobs:
  build:
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04

    steps:
      - name: Check out repository
        uses: actions/checkout@v4

      - name: Set up Node.js
        uses: actions/setup-node@v4
        with:
          node-version: 22

      - name: Build static settings page
        run: |
          npm run build:config:docs
          touch docs/.nojekyll

      - name: Upload Pages artifact
        uses: actions/upload-pages-artifact@v3
        with:
          path: docs

  deploy:
    needs: build
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
    environment:
      name: github-pages
      url: ${{ steps.deployment.outputs.page_url }}

    steps:
      - name: Deploy to GitHub Pages
        id: deployment
        uses: actions/deploy-pages@v4

````

# Bibble App Store Listing

## Listing Metadata

- Name: `Bibble`
- Version: `0.4.0`
- Category: `Tools & Utilities`
- Release: `Public`
- Support Email: `nick.b.ludwig@proton.me`
- Source: `https://github.com/nick1udwig/bibble`

## App Icon

Use [`assets/bibble-icon.png`](../assets/bibble-icon.png) for the store icon submission.

![App icon](../assets/bibble-icon.png)

## Listing Text

Read the King James Bible on Repebble core devices. Choose Gothic 14, 18, or 24 in regular or bold for scripture, while clear headers and large bold selection grids keep navigation readable on rectangular and round displays. Bibble downloads the KJV text into PebbleKit JS on startup, then streams and caches pages for smooth watch-side reading without bundling the full Bible in the watch app.

## Example Screens

Four high-impact screens are captured for each supported platform: book grid, chapter grid, verse grid, and reader. These captures use Gothic 18 Bold for the reader; Emery headers follow that profile, Gabbro headers use their compact round-screen profile, and selection grids use fixed Gothic 24 Bold.

### Emery

4. ![Emery reader](./screenshots/emery/04-reader.png)

### Gabbro

# Publishing Notes

## App Icon

Use [`assets/bibble-icon.png`](../assets/bibble-icon.png) as the app store submission icon.

The Pebble launcher/menu icon is bundled from [`resources/bibble-menu-icon.png`](../resources/bibble-menu-icon.png) through the `APP_ICON` resource in `package.json`.

Generated icon sizes:

- [`assets/bibble-icon.png`](../assets/bibble-icon.png): 1024x1024
- [`assets/bibble-icon-144.png`](../assets/bibble-icon-144.png): 144x144
- [`assets/bibble-icon-80.png`](../assets/bibble-icon-80.png): 80x80
- [`resources/bibble-menu-icon.png`](../resources/bibble-menu-icon.png): 25x25

## Build

```bash
npm run build:config:docs
npm test
npm run build:watch:release
```

Configure GitHub Pages to deploy from the `master` branch's `/docs` directory. Then verify the
configuration page at <https://nick1udwig.github.io/bibble/config/> after publishing.

The release build minifies the packaged companion JavaScript and omits its source map from the PBW. The matching map remains available at `build/release/pebble-js-app.js.map` for debugging.

## Phone Install

```bash
npm run deploy:phone
```

## Store Listing

Use [`docs/app-store-listing.md`](./app-store-listing.md) as the working source for store submission metadata.

Source: `scripts/generate-preview-fonts.py`

Git revision: `55236ff9ec2cbe30eba178856ea45c52f9771d1c`. SHA-256: `27471ee523ce80ae9f02485b2ae36d10e6dd3ce9944d316f9b88c85c6ac2f33a`.

Snapshot imported during KB initialization. The repository file remains the editable source of truth.

````
"""Extract ASCII bitmap glyphs from PebbleOS Gothic PBF fonts.

Usage: python scripts/generate-preview-fonts.py /path/to/pbf-files
Source: https://github.com/coredevices/PebbleOS/tree/main/resources
GOTHIC_14, GOTHIC_18_BOLD and GOTHIC_24 are in common/base/pbf;
the other variants are in normal/base/pbf. No font substitution or scaling.
"""
import json
from pathlib import Path
import struct
import sys

fonts = {}
for size in (14, 18, 24, 28):
    for bold in (False, True):
        data = (Path(sys.argv[1]) / ('GOTHIC_' + str(size) + ('_BOLD' if bold else '') + '.pbf')).read_bytes()
        version, height, count, wildcard, buckets, cp_bytes, header_size, features = struct.unpack_from('<BBHHBBBB', data)
        assert version == 3 and features == 1 and cp_bytes == 2, 'Expected uncompressed v3 font with 16-bit offsets'
        offsets = header_size + buckets * 4
        bitmaps = offsets + count * 4
        glyphs = {}
        for i in range(count):
            code, offset = struct.unpack_from('<HH', data, offsets + i * 4)
            if not 32 <= code <= 126:
                continue
            start = bitmaps + offset
            w, h, left, top, advance = struct.unpack_from('<BBbbb', data, start)
            pixels = data[start + 5:start + 5 + (w * h + 7) // 8]
            rows = [sum(((pixels[(y * w + x) // 8] >> ((y * w + x) % 8)) & 1) << x for x in range(w)) for y in range(h)]
            glyphs[chr(code)] = [w, h, left, top, advance, rows]
        assert len(glyphs) == 95
        fonts[str(size) + ('b' if bold else 'r')] = {'height': height, 'glyphs': glyphs}
Path('src/config/preview-fonts.js').write_text('// Generated by scripts/generate-preview-fonts.py from PebbleOS system fonts.\nwindow.BibblePreviewFonts = ' + json.dumps(fonts, separators=(',', ':')) + ';\n')

metrics = {key: {"height": font["height"],
                 "top": min(g[3] for g in font["glyphs"].values()),
                 "bottom": max(g[3] + g[1] for g in font["glyphs"].values()),
                 "glyphs": {ch: g[:5] for ch, g in font["glyphs"].items()}}
           for key, font in fonts.items()}
Path("src/common/font-metrics.js").write_text(
    "// Generated by scripts/generate-preview-fonts.py from PebbleOS system fonts.\n"
    "(function(root) { var metrics = " + json.dumps(metrics, separators=(",", ":")) +
    "; if (typeof module === \"object\") module.exports = metrics; else root.BibbleFontMetrics = metrics; }(this));\n")

````

#!/usr/bin/env bash
set -euo pipefail

script_dir="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)"
project_root="$(dirname "$script_dir")"
pbw="${1:-$project_root/build/bibble.pbw}"

if [[ ! -f "$pbw" ]]; then
  echo "PBW not found: $pbw" >&2
  exit 1
fi

pbw="$(realpath "$pbw")"
build_dir="$(dirname "$pbw")"
source_js="$build_dir/pebble-js-app.js"
source_map="$build_dir/pebble-js-app.js.map"
release_dir="$build_dir/release"
release_js="$release_dir/pebble-js-app.js"
release_map="$release_dir/pebble-js-app.js.map"

if [[ ! -f "$source_js" || ! -f "$source_map" ]]; then
  echo "Companion JavaScript build outputs were not found beside $pbw" >&2
  exit 1
fi

node "$script_dir/minify-release-js.mjs" "$source_js" "$source_map" "$release_js" "$release_map"

if unzip -p "$pbw" pebble-js-app.js.map >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  zip -q -d "$pbw" pebble-js-app.js.map >/dev/null
fi
zip -q -d "$pbw" pebble-js-app.js >/dev/null
zip -q -0 -j "$pbw" "$release_js"

if ! unzip -p "$pbw" pebble-js-app.js | cmp -s - "$release_js"; then
  echo "Packaged companion JavaScript does not match the minified release output" >&2
  exit 1
fi

debug_bytes="$(wc -c < "$source_js")"
release_bytes="$(wc -c < "$release_js")"
echo "Companion JavaScript: $debug_bytes -> $release_bytes bytes"
echo "External release source map: $release_map"
ls -lh "$pbw"

````

````
#
# Pebble application build rules.
#
import os.path

top = '.'
out = 'build'


def options(ctx):
    ctx.load('pebble_sdk')


def configure(ctx):
    ctx.load('pebble_sdk')


def build(ctx):
    ctx.load('pebble_sdk')

    build_worker = os.path.exists('worker_src')
    binaries = []

    cached_env = ctx.env
    for platform in ctx.env.TARGET_PLATFORMS:
        ctx.env = ctx.all_envs[platform]
        ctx.set_group(ctx.env.PLATFORM_NAME)
        app_elf = '{}/pebble-app.elf'.format(ctx.env.BUILD_DIR)
        ctx.pbl_build(source=ctx.path.ant_glob('src/c/**/*.c'), target=app_elf, bin_type='app')

        if build_worker:
            worker_elf = '{}/pebble-worker.elf'.format(ctx.env.BUILD_DIR)
            binaries.append({'platform': platform, 'app_elf': app_elf, 'worker_elf': worker_elf})
            ctx.pbl_build(source=ctx.path.ant_glob('worker_src/c/**/*.c'),
                          target=worker_elf,
                          bin_type='worker')
        else:
            binaries.append({'platform': platform, 'app_elf': app_elf})
    ctx.env = cached_env

    ctx.set_group('bundle')
    ctx.pbl_bundle(binaries=binaries,
                   js=ctx.path.ant_glob(['src/pkjs/**/*.js',
                                         'src/pkjs/**/*.json',
                                         'src/common/**/*.js']),
                   js_entry_file='src/pkjs/index.js')

````

documents.content:
Source: `README.md`

Git revision: `55236ff9ec2cbe30eba178856ea45c52f9771d1c`. SHA-256: `87bb67b814e2350b58c62c98544780e1a33b75a69b510f68a02c1d9b56bebad2`.

Snapshot imported during KB initialization. The repository file remains the editable source of truth.

# Bibble

KJV Bible reader for Repebble core devices.

Hold Select to query with dictation.
Speak a book/chapter/verse, or a phrase to search for in the text.

## Build

```sh
npm run fetch:kjv
npm run generate:data
npm run build:config:docs
npm test
npm run build:watch
```

The generated Bible file in the PBW contains metadata only.
The KJV text comes from [`nick1udwig/bible` on `master`](https://github.com/nick1udwig/bible/tree/master) (forked from [`thiagobodruk/bible`](https://github.com/thiagobodruk/bible)) and is cached persistently by PKJS after the first successful download.
Runtime downloads, data-generation provenance, fetch tooling, and cache versioning all use `src/common/kjv-source.js` as their source definition.

## Deploy

```sh
npm run deploy:phone
```

This builds `build/bibble.pbw` and installs it to the paired phone with `pebble install --phone`.

## App Description

The companion settings page at <https://nick1udwig.github.io/bibble/config/> lets the reader use Gothic 14, 18, 24, or 28 (Very large) in regular or bold, defaulting to 18 Bold.
Rectangular headers follow the reader profile; round headers use compact Gothic 14 Bold so the time and full reference remain inside the display. Selection grids stay at Gothic 24 Bold for consistent legibility.
Pages use the selected bitmap font’s glyph widths, descenders, and display geometry. Each screen packs as many whole verses as fit. A verse that does not fit the remaining rows starts on the next screen; only verses longer than a full screen continue across pages. The watch and settings preview share these line breaks.
Chapters are paginated lazily for the selected reader profile; changing it never rebuilds or redownloads the KJV corpus.

The native watch app is C.
On first use, PKJS downloads and normalizes the KJV text into compressed persistent phone-side storage, then immediately builds a compact, compressed, positional verse index.
Later launches restore the completed index and its decoded shards into memory without rebuilding or parsing the whole Bible.
Existing plaintext book caches migrate in place while an incompatible index is rebuilt once from the cached corpus, without redownloading it.
Search uses Lunr's finite-state term dictionary for bounded edit-distance matching, exact-first posting-list intersection, BM25 relevance, and index-resident phrase/proximity ranking.
Only the displayed hit verses are hydrated from the corpus.
PKJS also owns reference parsing and chapter paging.
The watch keeps an eight-entry LRU page cache and prefetches an asymmetric reading window (four pages forward and two backward) over AppMessage.

Holding Select starts dictation.
Spoken Bible references still navigate directly; other phrases search the full KJV.
Search results arrive five at a time, show a verse reference and compact excerpt with matching terms in bold, and open the selected verse when tapped or selected.

documents.title: Reading, typography, preview, and header requirements
documents.content:
These are the final requirements agreed in the user conversation on 2026-09-10 (America/Los_Angeles). Later clarifications supersede earlier approaches. This spec records intent; implementation and device validation are separate.

## Font choices
- Scripture font sizes are 14 (Compact), 18 (Medium, default), 24 (Large), and 28 (Very large).
- Every size supports regular and bold; default is 18 Bold.
- Very large uses the actual Pebble Gothic 28 regular/bold font, not a browser approximation.
- Persist and apply the user's selected size and boldness.

## Screen pagination and verse boundaries
- Text must not overflow the screen or leave a partially clipped line at any supported size/weight on either supported watch.
- Measure actual glyph widths and vertical bounds, including descenders that extend below the nominal font height. Account for header space, margins, and the circular display's changing usable width.
- Fill each page with as many complete verses as fit, in order. Each verse starts on a new line.
- If the next verse does not fit the remaining rows, start that verse at the top of the next screen. Leaving unused rows is correct when necessary to preserve the verse boundary.
- A page starts at a verse's beginning unless it continues a verse that is too long for a full fresh screen. Only such oversized verses split across pages.
- Continuations start at the top of the screen, preserve every character in order, and use complete fitting lines. Avoid splitting words when a word boundary is available.
- Navigation moves between complete screenfuls. A single touch swipe must not skip multiple pages as touch-movement events arrive.
- Size-specific character limits are not a valid substitute for measuring layout. Buffer capacity must accommodate a densely packed screen.
- Cache identity must distinguish watch geometry and font profile; chapter/verse lookup and adjacent-page navigation must remain correct after repagination.

Regression examples: John 3:16 at 24px fits a rectangular screen and must not be split after "have" merely by the former 135-character budget. At 28px it is too tall for one screen and must continue on a new page, with no clipped last line. When preceding verses leave insufficient room, move a fitting whole verse to a fresh screen.

## Preview
- Accurately reflect the supported watch shape, dimensions, glyphs, size, boldness, headers, margins, and the actual page breaks.
- Supported targets: emery / Pebble Time 2, 200 × 228 rectangular; gabbro / Pebble Round 2, 260 × 260 circular.
- Use the real bitmap fonts and the shared reader pagination engine.
- Default the model selector to the connected watch when available; allow previewing either target.
- Previous/Next preview controls show how a long verse continues.
- Rectangular headers follow the selected font profile; the current round design uses compact Gothic 14 Bold and a stacked time/reference header.

## Book grid
- Book abbreviation labels (Gen, Exo, Lev, etc.) follow the user's selected size and weight, matching scripture typography.
- Every label must fit inside its existing grid cell at every supported size. If a size does not fit, report that finding rather than asserting success or silently shrinking it.
- Scope was book labels. Chapter and verse selection grids retain their existing Gothic 24 Bold behavior.
- The experiment checked all 66 abbreviations: maximum width 41px versus minimum 64px available, and glyph height fits the 34px text frame. Both target builds passed; these are metric/build checks, not on-device visual proof.

## Reference headers
- Preserve the complete chapter number when a long book name overruns the header.
- Truncate only the book-name prefix, then append two dots, a space, and the number: e.g. `Lamentat.. 1` (the fitting prefix depends on font/weight).
- Keep the full book name when it fits. Preserve multi-digit chapter numbers as well.
- Apply this to reader and verse-selection headers containing a chapter reference; refresh on font changes.
- In the user's wording "book number" referred to the chapter number in the displayed reference, not the book's ordinal position in the Bible.

## Implementation and evidence
- [[code:src/common/reader-layout.js::paginate]] and [[code:src/common/reader-layout.js::geometry]] own fitting and verse-aware page construction.
- [[code:src/c/main.c::prv_reader_body_update]] renders the precomputed lines; [[code:src/c/main.c::prv_grid_draw]] selects the book-grid font; [[code:src/c/main.c::prv_fit_chapter_header]] preserves the chapter suffix.
- [[repo/files/tests/paging-test-js]], [[repo/files/tests/preview-test-js]], [[repo/files/tests/settings-test-js]] cover pagination, preview, and settings.
- Pagination and preview: `a69b0d8`; selected book-grid font: `416a40b`; chapter-preserving header: `55236ff`.
- Prior conversation reports: full tests passed; both watch targets built; browser previews visually checked; 10,701 header cases checked using the compiled formatter with font-metric stubs. No successful final hardware/emulator validation was established; the emulator install stalled and was stopped.

Related: [[decisions/pagination-evolution]], [[context/overridable/current-state]].
